UN Human Rights Committee grills Canada over mining, aboriginal treatment

The federal government is sidestepping a UN panel's request to explain how Canadian mining and resource companies deal with human rights complaints.

Tuesday was the Canadian government's first opportunity to address the UN Human Rights Committee in Geneva, which is conducting the first review in 10 years of Canada's compliance to a major international treaty.

The committee, comprised of 18 experts, heard repeated concerns about Canada's extractives industry, the treatment of aboriginals and anti-terrorism measures from two dozen groups, including the Canadian Human Rights Commission and Amnesty International.

Amnesty International, in its submission to the panel, argued that any human rights initiatives taken by companies are purely voluntary, and no enforceable code of conduct exists. It urged the committee to recommend a way for overseas litigants to pursue legal action in Canadian courts.

QB, Penn State, 6'4 236

Strengths:

  • Impressive arm, throws the ball with zip all over the field and can make any throw asked of him.

  • Excellent pocket presence and poise. Despite a very bad line he never looked rattled under constant siege.

  • Good mobility. Only takes off as a last resort and always has his eyes down field.

  • Moves in the pocket very well, navigates trash while keeping his eyes down field.

  • Has experience making pre and post snap reads in a pro style offense. Moves through progressions quickly.

  • Carried a very weak supporting cast to overachieve.

Weaknesses:

  • Maddeningly inconsistent accuracy. One drive it looks like he can place the ball anywhere he wants it, then the next he is missing open receivers by 10 yards.

  • Tends to stand flat footed at times and doesn't always have his feet set properly. Could be a reason for his accuracy issues.

  • Will hold the ball and throw dangerous passes or take sacks instead of throwing it away.

Overall: It is easy to see why people drool over the kid. At times he looks like a star day one starter. The problem is other times he looks like Tim Tebow. If he can continue to improve his footwork and fix his accuracy problems he is the hands down #1 pick if you need a quarterback. That is a big if however.

So r/web_dev was one of my most valued tools as a developer. It helped me grow and really gave me my career. I want to help make this subverse as good if not better than its predecessor. I was inspired by a discussion , and thought this would be the subverse to maybe help get content rolling here.

So my questions to you are:

  1. Should we look into a way to scrape some of the top links from subreddits and post them here?

  2. Is there anything you want done differently in this subverse?

Lastly, I really want to see voat grow and the biggest drawback I see now (aside from voat going down) is content. I think we can solve this.

Thanks for reading. Sorry if this isn't the right place for this.

I think manual curation is the way to go, rather than automatically scraping. Especially from Reddit. Voat needs to be its own site, with its own unique community. That's the only real way for it to grow.

That said, people need to post content. They need to comment. If we don't all contribute then this sub and Voat as a whole will fade away into obscurity.

I'd much rather Voat be smaller user base wise then it grow as large as reddit. Like flies on shit popularity isn't always a great thing as it attracts the wrong kind of crowd. Slashdot is a great example of what the Voat community should be like, but this would be solely my own take on all of this.

As with most well developed subs on Reddit, I was totally pleased by the content and direction of /r/webdev. The vibe was pleasant and not nearly as tough as /r/frontend, which is more than happy to tell you what you're doing is stupid.

I say the name of this sub is the same and the vibe should, naturally, contiune.

Not sure if scraping is needed, though not sure if it would diminish the integrity of this new space either, at least until it reaches critical mass and maintains stability as far as hosting.

That said, I am more willing to submit content here to help bolster the cache of info offered.
